parsed.why: Moderate-tier division: no adult facility ban, documents changeable, marriage equality; but no statewide gender-identity nondiscrimination or hate-crime coverage and youth-targeting through boards. Slightly above parent on facilities, held down by thin recourse.

Among worst states for anti-trans legislation: birth-certificate surgical requirement forces document disclosure, 2023 law permits bathroom restriction in state-run facilities, youth-care ban, no nondiscrimination or hate-crime protection. Adds a hostile layer below the parent.

Low-risk tier with operative protections: statewide gender-identity discrimination ban, X markers on licences, gender-neutral bathrooms required, sanctuary-city shield, vetoed sports and care bans. National passport and entry regime still applies, capping the score.

Low-risk tier: no facility bans, repeated gubernatorial vetos of care and sports bans, prison hormones upheld; but surgery-required document changes, no X marker, patchy local ordinances (21% coverage), no statewide gender-identity protection or hate-crime coverage.

Criminalises bathroom use not matching birth sex in government buildings and private businesses, misdemeanour up to a year, effective July 2026; suit pending, no established remedy. Plus barred birth-certificate change, sports ban, parent-disclosure mandate. Worst tier-1 exposure.
